The Department of Energy/National Nuclear Security Administration (DOE/NNSA) Stockpile Stewardship and Man- agement Plan (SSMP) identifies the DARHT facility as a weapons mission–critical facility and states that there is a need to modernize DARHT to support weapons modernization efforts [NNSA, 2022]. DARHT must be maintained and the facility modernized to enable the NNSA to continue delivering “a safe, secure, and effective deterrent,” thereby retaining this singular capability and ensuring an adaptive nuclear security enterprise [DOD, 2022]. The 2018 Nuclear Posture Review (NPR) states that the nuclear weapons infrastructure has suffered the effects of age and underfunding with no margin for further delay in recapitalizing the physical infrastructure [DOD, 2018]. The 2022 NPR further reinforced that strategic, integrated deterrence must incorporate modernization of the science and technology base [DOD, 2022]. Finally, the 2022 Enhanced Mission Delivery Initiative recommends that the NNSA “embark upon a strategic plan for the maintenance and recapitalization of the RDT&E [research, development, test, and evaluation] infrastructure.” [NNSA EMDI, 2022] Conceived in the 1970s, constructed in the 1990s. and opera- tional since 2000, DARHT is an integral part of the physical RDT&E infrastructure cited by both the Department of Defense (DOD) and the DOE, and has become indispensable for the certification of the primaries of U.S. nuclear weapons. The capability and capacity of the DARHT facility to meet NNSA needs is currently threatened by aging infrastructure, obsolescent technology, and increasingly challenging measurement requirements. To address these threats, NNSA has determined that the aging facility, accelerators, vessels, detector systems, and DARHT-supporting infrastructure require modernization. Prioritization of “crucial NNSA infrastructure modernization programs is the best and only option to pace projected threats and sustain strategic deterrence.” [HASC, 2022] This DARHT Capability eXpansion (DCX) strategy has been developed to implement NNSA requirements for sustainment and modernization to ensure DARHT continues to serve its role as a weapons mission–critical facility.
